name: HCG (human chorionic gonadotropin)
used_for: hCG is a glycoprotein hormone (alpha and beta subunits) made by the placenta that acts like LH. FDA-labeled products (Novarel, Pregnyl) are approved for prepubertal cryptorchidism, selected cases of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in men, and ovulation induction in women, and the label states hCG has not been demonstrated effective for obesity. It is also used off label alongside testosterone therapy to maintain testicular function and fertility. The FDA states there is no substantial evidence it increases weight loss, and over-the-counter hCG diet products are treated as illegal. hCG is a large protein hormone rather than a small peptide, and appears on sports anti-doping lists.

entries.text: Label: Novarel (chorionic gonadotropin) for prepubertal cryptorchidism not due to anatomical obstruction lists regimens advocated by various authorities, including 4,000 USP Units intramuscularly three times weekly for three weeks, or 500 to 1,000 USP Units per injection in other regimens.
entries.population: Prepubertal boys with cryptorchidism not due to anatomical obstruction

entries.text: Label: Novarel for selected cases of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in males lists 500 to 1,000 USP Units intramuscularly three times a week for three weeks, then the same dose twice a week for three weeks, or 4,000 USP Units three times weekly for six to nine months.
entries.population: Adult males with selected cases of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

internet_entries.text: An AI health information platform (Doctronic) says hCG alongside testosterone therapy is commonly given as 250 to 500 IU subcutaneously two to three times per week, and cites 1,500 to 3,000 IU three times weekly for fertility restoration.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: A private urology clinic blog says hCG for maintenance during testosterone therapy is commonly 500 to 1,000 IU subcutaneously 2 to 3 times per week, and 1,500 to 3,000 IU every other day for fertility recovery.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: A telehealth referral site with affiliate links says hCG maintenance on testosterone therapy is commonly 500 IU subcutaneously 2 to 3 times per week, and 1,000 to 1,500 IU every other day for fertility recovery.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: The Novarel label states it is for intramuscular use only and is supplied as a freeze-dried powder with bacteriostatic water diluent containing benzyl alcohol.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Novarel label states the unreconstituted product is stored at controlled room temperature (20 to 25 C), and the reconstituted product is refrigerated at 2 to 8 C and used within 30 days.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Novarel label states the regimens it lists are those advocated by various authorities and that the regimen depends on the indication, age, weight and physician preference.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: In a randomized trial comparing clomiphene, hCG injections and a combination in men with hypogonadism wishing to preserve fertility, testosterone rose in all three groups, with no significant difference in testosterone response among groups.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Wikipedia says hCG is extracted from the urine of pregnant women or produced by recombinant methods, and is used in assisted reproduction and to maintain fertility during testosterone replacement therapy.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: The Novarel label lists headache, irritability, restlessness, depression, fatigue, edema, precocious puberty, gynecomastia and injection site pain, and states hypersensitivity reactions, local and systemic, have been reported.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Novarel label lists contraindications including precocious puberty, prostatic carcinoma or other androgen-dependent neoplasm, and prior allergic reaction to hCG, and states hCG may cause fetal harm in pregnancy.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The FDA states that people following the very low calorie diets recommended with hCG weight-loss products face risks including gallstones, electrolyte imbalance and heart arrhythmias, and that it has received reports of serious adverse events including pulmonary embolism, depression, cerebrovascular events, cardiac arrest and death.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: Wikipedia notes that Albert Simeons's 'hCG diet' paired hCG with extreme calorie restriction, that the FDA requires a disclaimer that there is no substantial evidence hCG increases weight loss, and that over-the-counter hCG products were banned as fraudulent in December 2011.
Wikipedia notes professional athletes have been banned after testing positive for hCG, which is on banned-substance lists because it can restore testosterone production after steroid use.
Wikipedia says hCG triggers ovulation in women and stimulates testosterone production in men, and is used in assisted reproduction and to maintain fertility during testosterone replacement.

research.summary: FDA DailyMed prescribing information for Novarel (chorionic gonadotropin) for injection, Ferring, revised September 2025.
research.finding: Labeled for prepubertal cryptorchidism, selected hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in men, and ovulation induction; the label states hCG has not been demonstrated effective for obesity.

research.summary: FDA questions and answers page on hCG products for weight loss (content current as of May 2016).
research.finding: States there is no substantial evidence hCG increases weight loss, that homeopathic OTC hCG weight-loss products are illegal, and that hCG is approved only as an injectable for some female infertility and male hormonal conditions.

research.summary: Double-blind placebo-controlled trial of hCG injections plus a restricted diet in 40 obese women for 6 weeks.
research.finding: hCG showed no advantage over placebo for weight loss, hunger or other measures; the authors concluded there is no rationale for hCG injections in obesity.

research.summary: Randomized double-blind trial in 51 women of hCG versus placebo with the same low calorie diet over 32 days.
research.finding: No significant difference in weight loss, circumference or hunger between hCG and placebo.

research.summary: Randomized trial in 282 men with hypogonadism wishing to preserve fertility, comparing clomiphene, hCG, and both.
research.finding: All three arms raised testosterone with no significant difference among groups; the combination had a greater symptom score gain.

research.summary: Randomized trial in 29 healthy men given 200 mg testosterone enanthate weekly plus placebo or 125, 250 or 500 IU hCG every other day for 3 weeks (Coviello et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Testosterone alone cut testosterone inside the testes by 94%. Doses of 250 and 500 IU hCG every other day kept it near or above baseline, and it rose in line with the hCG dose.

research.summary: Randomized trial in 37 healthy men with experimentally induced gonadotropin deficiency testing very low hCG exposures on intratesticular testosterone.
research.finding: Intratesticular testosterone rose in a dose-dependent way with hCG, indicating hCG can stimulate testicular testosterone production in this experimental model.

dose.summary: The Novarel label lists regimens by indication, from 500 to 1,000 USP Units per injection up to 4,000 to 5,000 USP Units, all by muscle injection. Trials in men used 15 to 125 IU under the skin every other day, or 5,000 IU twice weekly. Online sources give lower under-the-skin doses for use with testosterone therapy (250 to 1,000 IU, 2 to 3 times a week), which differ from the label route. Diet doses of 125 IU a day are online claims, and the label says hCG has not been shown to help weight loss.

items.text: Label: Novarel for prepubertal cryptorchidism (undescended testicles) lists 4,000 USP Units three times weekly for three weeks, 5,000 USP Units every second day for four injections, 15 injections of 500 to 1,000 USP Units over six weeks, or 500 USP Units three times weekly for four to six weeks, then 1,000 USP Units per injection if a second course is needed a month later.
items.label: research

items.text: Label: Novarel for selected cases of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in men lists 500 to 1,000 USP Units three times a week for three weeks, then twice a week for three weeks, or 4,000 USP Units three times weekly for six to nine months, then possibly 2,000 USP Units three times weekly for three more months.
items.label: research

items.text: Label: for ovulation induction in women pretreated with menotropins, 5,000 to 10,000 USP Units one day after the last menotropin dose. The label says the regimen depends on indication, age, weight and physician preference.
items.label: research

items.text: In a randomized trial of 282 men with hypogonadism who wanted to preserve fertility, 5,000 IU hCG injections twice weekly raised testosterone as much as clomiphene (50 mg) did over 3 months.
items.label: research

items.text: In 29 healthy men on testosterone enanthate, 250 IU hCG every other day kept testosterone inside the testes near baseline and 500 IU raised it above baseline over 3 weeks. 125 IU was not enough.
items.label: research

items.text: In 37 healthy men with experimentally blocked gonadotropins, 15, 60 and 125 IU hCG under the skin every other day for 10 days raised testosterone inside the testes in a dose-dependent way.
items.label: research

items.text: In a 6-week trial of 40 obese women, daily muscle injections of hCG (6 days a week) worked no better than saline on weight loss or hunger.
items.label: research

fasting.summary: The label has no food rules. For weight loss, the label says hCG has no known effect on fat mobilization, appetite or hunger and no proven added benefit beyond calorie restriction. Two placebo-controlled trials found no benefit, and online diet plans pair hCG with about 500 calories a day.

items.text: Label: hCG has no known effect on fat mobilization, appetite or hunger, or body fat distribution, and there is no substantial evidence it increases weight loss beyond calorie restriction. The label has no food or fasting instructions for its approved uses.
items.label: research

frequency.summary: The label regimens run from every second day to three times a week, and twice a week later in treatment. The label has no missed-dose rule. Online sources suggest two to three times a week with testosterone therapy and a missed-dose rule that is untested.

items.text: Label regimens range from three times weekly (500 to 4,000 USP Units) and every second day (5,000 USP Units, four injections) to twice a week after three weeks in the hypogonadism regimen. The label gives no instruction for a missed dose.
items.label: research

items.text: In the 282-man trial, 5,000 IU hCG was given twice weekly for 3 months.
items.label: research

items.text: In the healthy-men trials hCG was given every other day (125, 250 or 500 IU for 3 weeks, or 15 to 125 IU for 10 days).
items.label: research

items.text: Doctronic says a Monday and Thursday split is a practical starting point, and three times weekly is preferred when fertility is the goal.

cycle_length.summary: The label courses last 3 to 6 weeks for cryptorchidism and up to 9 to 12 months for hypogonadism, and says testicular descent is usually reversible when hCG stops. Trials ran 10 days to 3 months. Online sources describe 3 to 12 months for fertility and 23 or 40 days for diets.

items.text: Label: the cryptorchidism courses last 3 to 6 weeks, and a second course may follow a month later. The hypogonadism regimen runs 6 weeks, or 6 to 9 months with possibly 3 more months at a lower dose.
items.label: research

items.text: Label: testicular descent from hCG is usually reversible when hCG is discontinued, and in most cases the response is temporary.
items.label: research

items.text: Trials were short: 3 months in 282 men with hypogonadism, 3 weeks in healthy men on testosterone, 10 days in men with experimentally blocked gonadotropins, and 6 weeks and 32 days in the two weight-loss trials.

storage_and_handling.summary: The label says muscle injection only. Store the powder at room temperature, then refrigerate after mixing with bacteriostatic water and use within 30 days. Online guides describe under-the-skin injections, refrigerating the powder, and 60 days of stability, which differ from the label.

items.text: The Novarel label states it is for intramuscular use only and is supplied as a freeze-dried powder with bacteriostatic water diluent containing 0.9% benzyl alcohol. The label also asks for a visual check for particles and discoloration before use.

mechanism.summary: hCG acts like luteinizing hormone (LH). It makes the testes produce testosterone and, in women, triggers ovulation and supports the corpus luteum.

items.text: Label: hCG acts virtually like pituitary LH, with a small degree of FSH activity. It stimulates Leydig cells in the testis to make androgens and the ovarian corpus luteum to make progesterone, and can substitute for the mid-cycle LH surge that triggers ovulation.
items.label: research

items.text: In healthy men with blocked gonadotropins, testosterone inside the testes rose in line with hCG dose, showing hCG drives testicular testosterone directly.
items.label: research

items.text: Wikipedia says hCG triggers ovulation in women and stimulates testosterone production in men, and is used in assisted reproduction and to maintain fertility during testosterone replacement.
items.label: internet

items.text: Wikipedia says hCG is often used during testosterone replacement to restore or maintain fertility and prevent testicular shrinkage.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: hCG raises testosterone in men with low testosterone: in a 282-man trial it raised testosterone about 2.2-fold over 3 months, matching clomiphene. For weight loss, the trials found no benefit over placebo.

items.text: In 282 men with hypogonadism who wanted to keep fertility, 5,000 IU hCG twice weekly raised testosterone over 3 months, similar to clomiphene alone or with hCG (average testosterone across all groups rose from 2.31 to 5.17 nmol/L, still below the normal range).
items.label: research

items.text: In healthy men on testosterone enanthate, testosterone inside the testes fell 94% on placebo, but 250 to 500 IU hCG every other day for 3 weeks held it near or above baseline.
items.label: research

items.text: For weight loss, two double-blind trials (40 and 51 women) found no difference from placebo, and the label says hCG has not been shown to help obesity.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Warnings
side_effect_groups.summary: The label lists contraindications and serious risks in women treated with menotropins, including ovarian hyperstimulation and blood clots.

items.text: The Novarel label lists contraindications including precocious puberty, prostatic carcinoma or other androgen-dependent neoplasm, and prior allergic reaction to hCG, and states hCG may cause fetal harm in pregnancy.
items.label: research

items.text: Label warnings with menotropins: ovarian hyperstimulation, ovarian cyst enlargement or rupture, multiple births and arterial thromboembolism. Anaphylaxis has been reported with urinary-derived hCG, and there are sporadic reports of testicular tumors in young men treated for infertility, with no proven cause.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.summary: The FDA warns that the very low calorie diets used with hCG weight-loss products carry risks, including serious events.
